name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
summary: German mathematician, astronomer, and physicist known for contributions to number theory, statistics, analysis, differential geometry, geodesy, geophysics, electrostatics, astronomy, and optics.

name: Axel D. Wittmann
summary: Author of the source document, affiliated with Institut für Astrophysik, University of Göttingen.

name: University of Göttingen
summary: University in Göttingen, Germany, where Gauss studied and later worked.

name: Göttingen Astronomical Observatory
summary: Astronomical observatory in Göttingen directed by Gauss from 1807.

name: Gauss Society
summary: Registered association founded in Göttingen in 1962 to preserve the memory of Gauss.

name: Brunswick
summary: City in Germany where Gauss was born.

name: Helmstedt
summary: City in Germany where Gauss received his doctoral degree.

name: Göttingen
summary: City in Germany where Gauss studied and worked.

name: Johanna Osthoff
summary: First wife of Carl Friedrich Gauss.

name: Wilhelmine Waldeck
summary: Second wife of Carl Friedrich Gauss.

name: Wilhelm Weber
summary: Physicist who collaborated with Gauss on magnetism and the electromagnetic telegraph.

name: Giuseppe Piazzi
summary: Italian astronomer who observed Ceres on 1 January 1801.

name: Franz Xaver von Zach
summary: Astronomer who rediscovered Ceres in December 1801 using Gauss's calculations.

name: Carl Wilhelm Ferdinand
summary: Duke of Brunswick who sponsored Gauss's education.

name: Ceres Ferdinandea
summary: Dwarf planet rediscovered in 1801 using Gauss's orbit calculations.

name: Disquisitiones arithmeticae
summary: Gauss's main mathematical monograph published in 1801.

name: Theoria Motus Corporum Coelestium
summary: Gauss's important monograph in astronomy published in 1809.

name: Heliotrope
summary: Device invented by Gauss to direct sunlight with arcsecond accuracy for surveying.

name: Electromagnetic telegraph
summary: First fully operational electromagnetic telegraph invented by Gauss and Weber in 1833.

name: Julius Bartels
summary: Geophysicist and first president of the Gauss Society.

name: Horst Michling
summary: Head of the geodesy department of the Göttingen town administration and founder of the Gauss Society.
